standard_prerequisites: The definition of the intersection number of invertible sheaves with an integral closed subspace, and its agreement with the leading term of the corresponding numerical polynomial
The decomposition of a cycle into the classes of its irreducible components with multiplicities

Chow's lemma producing a proper morphism that is an isomorphism over a dense open subspace and whose source is a scheme, the compatibility of intersection numbers with pullback, and the projection formula for capping with a first Chern class
core_obligations: Decompose the class of the closed subspace into the classes of its components of the relevant dimension weighted by multiplicities

Observe that the iterated cap of the first Chern classes is additive over that decomposition, and that the same decomposition holds for the intersection number by the numerical polynomial leading term statement
Reduce to the case of a proper integral algebraic space over the base field

Use Chow's lemma to replace it by a proper scheme, shrinking the source to the closure of the preimage of a dense open subspace so that it stays integral; check that both the intersection number and the iterated cap are unchanged by this replacement, the latter through the projection formula
Conclude by the scheme case of the statement
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an integral case by decomposing into components with multiplicities
Pass to a proper scheme by Chow's lemma, keeping integrality and both sides unchanged
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the comparison between intersection numbers and degrees of iterated Chern class caps at source lines 5212-5226, label lemma-degrees-and-numerical-intersections, whose proof occupies source lines 5228-5265. The proof first reduces to an integral space by decomposing the cycle into its components with multiplicities and invoking the same decomposition for the intersection number through the leading term of the numerical polynomial, and then does real geometric work: Chow's lemma supplies a proper morphism that is an isomorphism over a dense open subspace and has a scheme as source, the source is replaced by the scheme theoretic closure of the preimage of that open subspace so that it remains integral, and both sides are checked to be unchanged, the cycle side through the projection formula for capping with a first Chern class. The scheme case is then quoted. The counted statement records neither the decomposition nor the passage to a scheme.
